acceptance: A refresh PR whose required checks pass is merged by the controller without a manual dispatch or waiting for the next schedule.
The triggered path re-reads live state and refuses a moved head, changed marker or failing check, with tests in tests/test_downstream_controller.py.
BENCHBOX_UPSTREAM_ENABLED unset or a dry run performs no merge.
context: Fork PR #86 merged 4e518548. Required workflow completion events trigger merge-only plans, filtered by canonical event/repo/branch/head and live ownership/check gates. All 20 contexts passed. Actual workflow_run merge awaits next real refresh; no claim of observed event-driven merge.
description:
Problem. In BenchBox-dev/benchbox-sqlglot, .github/workflows/benchbox-upstream.yml (downstream/controller.py) runs daily at 05:41 UTC. One run opens the refresh PR; merging it after the fork's 20 required checks pass needs another controller run. Observed for v30.30.0: run 42323862808 opened fork PR #85; its checks passed about 10 minutes later; the merge happened only because run 42324868577 was dispatched by hand. Unattended, the merge waits up to 24 h, and the core adoption (see sqlglot-delivery-arm-waits-for-daily-run-20261107) waits another day. Fork-repository work: changes land through a fork PR, not a BenchBox PR.

Change. Trigger the controller's merge step when the refresh PR's required checks complete (for example workflow_run on the fork's required workflows, filtered to refresh/upstream-* heads), keeping the read-only prepare job, the App-token-only publish job, live re-reads before every action and the kill switch.
